newsitem.title: INDIA: India's October foodgrain stocks fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: India's October foodgrain stocks fall sharply.

text.p: India held foodgrain stocks of 19.6 million tonnes as of October 1, compared with 29.9 million on the same date last year, a Food Ministry statement said on Wednesday.
The government had prescribed a foodgrain buffer stock requirement of 16.6 million tonnes as of October 1.
The statement said wheat procurement by government agencies in 1996/97 (April-March) fell to 8.18 million tonnes from 12.33 million in the previous year due to a fall in output.
India produced 62.6 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97, against 65.7 million tonnes last year.

"It is hoped that despite lower level of procurement of wheat in 1996/97 season, it would be possible to maintain the stocks more or less at the prescribed buffer norms level on April 1, 1997," the statement said.
The foodgrains buffer requirement stipulated by the government for April 1 is 14.5 million tonnes.
The statement said rice procurement in 1996/97 was expected to be 12 million tonnes compared with 9.9 million previously.
